projects.title: Matrix Multiplication & Dimension Validator
projects.description: Write a C program that validates matrix compatibility (columns of A == rows of B) and multiplies two 2D matrices A and B.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. Validate that c1 == r2.
2. Iterate triple nested loops: outer i (rows of A), middle j (cols of B), inner k (common dimension).
3. Accumulate C[i][j] += A[i][k] * B[k][j].
projects.codeExplanation: Demonstrates robust 2D array processing, boundary checking, and the standard O(N^3) matrix dot-product multiplication algorithm.

projects.title: Class Marksheet Statistical Ranker & Median Finder
projects.description: Sort an array of student marks in descending order using Selection Sort, then compute total students, class mean, median, highest, lowest, and formatted merit rank scoreboard.
projects.exampleOutput:
Highest: 95 (Rank 1)
Lowest: 45 (Rank 9)
Mean: 73.78
Median: 78.00
Rank 1: 95
Rank 2: 92...
projects.logicExplanation:
1. Apply Selection Sort tracking max index per pass to order descending.
2. Sum elements and divide by n for mean.
3. Compute median based on odd/even length indexing.
projects.codeExplanation: Demonstrates in-place sorting, statistical aggregation, and floating-point average computations on integer sequences.

projects.title: In-Place Array Reversal and Right Rotation by K Positions
projects.description: Rotate an array to the right by k positions in O(n) linear time and O(1) auxiliary space using the 3-step reversal algorithm.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. Reverse entire array (0 to n-1).
2. Reverse first k elements (0 to k-1).
3. Reverse remaining n-k elements (k to n-1).
projects.codeExplanation: Demonstrates the two-pointer in-place reversal technique and optimal cyclic array rotation without allocating auxiliary buffer arrays.

projects.title: Subarray with Given Sum Finder (Sliding Window)
projects.description: Find a contiguous subarray whose elements sum to a target value S in O(n) linear time using the two-pointer sliding window technique.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. Maintain window sum from start to end.
2. Expand end pointer adding elements; shrink start pointer when sum exceeds target.
3. Return indices when currentSum == target.
projects.codeExplanation: Demonstrates sliding window algorithm optimizing an otherwise O(n^2) brute-force search into O(n) linear time.

projects.title: Spiral Matrix Traversal Engine
projects.description: Traverse and print all elements of an M x N 2D matrix in clockwise spiral order.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. Define 4 boundary variables: top, bottom, left, right.
2. Loop four directional sweeps (right, down, left, up), advancing boundary offsets after each traversal.
projects.codeExplanation: Demonstrates complex 2D boundary tracking and algorithmic matrix coordinate traversal.

projects.title: Matrix Transpose & Symmetry Verifier
projects.description: Verify whether a square matrix is symmetric (A[i][j] == A[j][i]) by comparing upper and lower triangles.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. Ensure matrix is square (ROWS == COLS).
2. Loop i from 0 to N-1 and j from i+1 to N-1; if A[i][j] != A[j][i], return 0.
projects.codeExplanation: Demonstrates triangular loop bounds (j = i + 1) to avoid redundant comparisons when verifying matrix symmetry.

projects.title: Second Largest & Smallest Elements in Single Pass O(n)
projects.description: Find the second largest and second smallest distinct numbers in an array in a single linear pass without sorting.
projects.exampleOutput: Largest: 35, Second Largest: 34, Smallest: 1, Second Smallest: 10
projects.logicExplanation:
1. Track firstMax and secondMax initialized to INT_MIN.
2. If current > firstMax, update secondMax = firstMax, firstMax = current.
3. Else if current > secondMax and current != firstMax, update secondMax = current.
projects.codeExplanation: Demonstrates linear single-pass tracking using INT_MIN / INT_MAX from <limits.h>.

projects.title: Array Frequency Counter & Duplicate Filter
projects.description: Count the frequency of each distinct element in an array and print the unique filtered array.
projects.exampleOutput:
4 appears 3 times, 5 appears 2 times...
Filtered Unique: [ 4, 5, 2, 8, 9, 7 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. Maintain a boolean visited array.
2. For each unvisited element, count identical occurrences in subsequent indices and mark visited.
projects.codeExplanation: Demonstrates counting and duplicate filtering using frequency marker arrays.

projects.title: Matrix Saddle Point Detector
projects.description: Find a saddle point in a 2D matrix (an element that is the minimum in its row and maximum in its column).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. For each row i, find column index with minimum element.
2. Verify if this minimum element is the maximum in that column across all rows.
projects.codeExplanation: Demonstrates multi-stage matrix coordinate verification and minimax condition checking.

projects.title: Polynomial Addition using 1D Array Representation
projects.description: Represent two algebraic polynomials A(x) and B(x) using 1D coefficient arrays where index represents power, and compute their sum polynomial.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. Array index i stores the coefficient for term x^i.
2. Add corresponding array indices: Sum[i] = A[i] + B[i].
3. Print formatted polynomial string with exponents.
projects.codeExplanation: Demonstrates mathematical data representation in 1D arrays and algebraic addition routines.
